So we’re all grateful to George Washington. A true mazel tov while he plopped around the Delaware without even a hairdresser waiting for him.

None of the definitions of Thanksgiving mentions the cranky in-laws, stuffed turkey, gravy, cranberry sauce, room-temperature veggies, first course, wine, cake, washing up, cracked dishes, pesky kids and days of work beforehand.

But some celebrities have said:

Uma Thurman: “The family comes over. Maybe I can’t cook everything, but I at least doctor the stuff up.”

Lorraine Bracco: “Forget turkey. I prefer pastrami and eggs. That’s my favorite, no matter what holiday.”

Amy Irving: “Ron Rifkin’s wife once made turkey loaf. Best Thanksgiving dinner my husband said he ever had. So that’s what I’ll do this year: turkey loaf.”

It’s our Day. Our heritage. Our country. Our gratitude. Our history. Our appreciation, thanks. Turkeys are native US birds. Not that anyone cares, but be it known there were never turkeys native to Turkey. Why would there be when Turkey has kebabs and baklava? So far, they still don’t have that in Allentown, Penn.

Everyone, may God bless us and this country.

news.originalContent:
Fighting near DRC hospital disrupts Ebola efforts, putting patients and workers at ‘grave risk’, WHO warns.

The World ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Health Organization (WHO) chief has urged peace following heavy fighting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) northeastern province, the epicentre of the Ebola outbreak.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠on ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Sunday that fighting near a hospital in the DRC’s Ituri ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠province disrupted Ebola response efforts and forced health workers and aid partners to shelter ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠inside a maternity ward for more than 24 hours.

“Heavy fighting has been ongoing since yesterday in the vicinity of a hospital in Ituri – in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged,” Tedros said on X.

“The situation has disrupted the work of the hospital and the wider Ebola response, putting patients, families and health workers at grave risk.”

Medical staff have been sheltering for their lives in a maternity ward in the facility for more than 24 hours, and the WHO is working to arrange a safe exit for the team and “for the hospital facilities, staff and patients to be protected,” Tedros also said.

“The best medicine is peace,” he added.

As of November 17, the WHO reported a total of 5,678 deaths out of 11,613 cases in the DRC, the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country.

The WHO said in a statement on Saturday that “while some areas had seen a slight decline in cases, sustained, high-level transmission continues overall in the country.”

Ituri and North Kivu, in the eastern part of the DRC, remain the most affected provinces.

The virus, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids, has spread across swaths of the DRC’s east and northeast, which have been plagued by violence for more than 30 years.

Earlier in November, armed men thought to be linked to an ISIL (ISIS)-affiliated group raided villages and killed dozens of people in North Kivu, forcing ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠patients with confirmed and suspected Ebola infections to flee.

The outbreak is also occurring amid ongoing fighting between government forces and the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group, which has seized key cities in eastern DRC, making transport of healthcare resources to remote regions difficult.

news.originalContent:
Stocks fall in South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong amid tech-led sell-off.

Asian stock markets have opened to sharp losses amid mounting concerns over the sustainability of the AI boom.

Key indexes in South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong fell on Monday, continuing Friday’s tech-led sell-off on both sides of the Pacific.

The Korea Composite Stock Price Index (Kospi) fell as much as 4.3 percent in early trading, while the Taiwan Stock Exchange Capitalization Weighted Stock Index (Taiex) and the Hang Seng Index both dipped more than 1 percent.

Japan’s stock markets were closed for Labor Thanksgiving Day.

On Friday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P500 closed 3.7 percent lower for its seventh straight loss, while the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3 percent to erase all of its gains for 2026, following a rout in Asia.

The Kospi, Nikkei 225, and the Taiex entered the weekend between 5.1 percent and 6.2 percent lower, while the Hang Seng Index finished down 1.9 percent.

Investors have long been concerned that tech firms may not be able to sustain the multi-trillion-dollar investments they have poured into the infrastructure needed to train and run AI.

Global AI-related investment, much of it fuelled by debt, is expected to reach $2.7 trillion in 2026 and $3.6 trillion in 2027, according to technology insights company Gartner.

Concerns that the AI boom may be running out of stream have been exacerbated by growing calls for greater oversight of the sector.

The Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the US midterm elections is expected to slow data centre construction in US states, while the alleged espionage scandal embroiling chip giant Nvidia and its former CEO Jensen Huang has led to a push for tighter restrictions on China’s access to advanced chips.

news.originalContent:
Cameroon’s former rebels face arrest fears and failed reintegration.

Douala, Cameroon – Collins Mbah says he hunted down and killed several Cameroonian soldiers in the English-speaking Northwest region during his time as a separatist fighter between 2016 and 2020. Today, in the coastal city of Douala, the man in his mid-30s, who went by the name Commander No Sorrow, has taken on a different role: traditional healer, tending to lives rather than taking them.

Mbah says he abandoned the armed struggle after realising that fellow fighters were turning against the very people they had set out to protect. But he has firmly ruled out joining the government’s disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration (DDR) programme.

“Quitting the struggle and joining the government disarmament programme would have meant I betrayed the people,” said Mbah, who dropped out of secondary school to join the revolt. “I don’t want to have anything to do with the government or the struggle any more. All I need now is peace of mind,” he told Al Jazeera.

October marked a decade since protests erupted in Cameroon’s English-speaking Northwest and Southwest regions, eventually escalating into an armed conflict between separatist fighters and government forces.

The unrest began in late 2016 after Anglophone lawyers and teachers protested against the appointment of Francophone magistrates unfamiliar with British common law to courts in English-speaking regions, and French-speaking teachers unable to communicate fluently in English to schools there. The protests were met with a government crackdown and eventually gave rise to a separatist movement seeking independence for the two regions, which its supporters call “Ambazonia”.

The conflict has killed thousands of people, displaced hundreds of thousands and disrupted education across the two English-speaking regions, according to humanitarian and human rights organisations. New figures released in October by the Cameroonian nonprofit Centre for Human Rights and Democracy in Africa (CHRDA) suggest the death toll could be as high as 10,000.

The fighting remains deadlocked, with separatist groups continuing attacks and kidnappings while the government pursues a military campaign. Alongside its military operations, the government has launched a community dialogue initiative, after distancing itself from Swiss- and Canadian-supported peace efforts.

Prime Minister Joseph Dion Ngute launched the initiative in Buea, the capital of Southwest, in September and in Bamenda, the capital of the Northwest, on October 15. Local leaders are being encouraged to persuade fighters to surrender and enter DDR centres. At the two events, 55 fighters – 25 in the Southwest and 30 in the Northwest – were presented as having renounced the armed struggle.

Despite leaving the rebellion, Mbah says he remains on the government’s wanted list. Without a national identity card, the father of three struggles to move freely around Douala and occasionally ventures into the outskirts to collect traditional herbs.

“I was initiated into traditional healing during childhood. The amulets and concoctions helped me foresee any danger when I was on the war front. Today, I use the same to heal,” he said. “But I don’t stay in a particular neighbourhood for long – I always move to the next to avoid being caught.”

Mbah is among former fighters who have chosen to reintegrate into society independently rather than enter government-run rehabilitation centres. Many say they fear arrest or poor treatment if they surrender.

Peter Mosongo, 28, now works as a motorcycle taxi rider in Buea after leaving the struggle in 2019. He joined in 2018 to protect his family but quit after witnessing what he describes as the indiscriminate killing of civilians by fellow fighters.

“I received threats from the fighters when I quit. They even kidnapped my father to force him to produce me,” Mosongo said. “I didn’t join DDR upon quitting out of fear that I may end up in prison. It was also being rumoured that those who surrendered were being killed silently.”

Mosongo says he also lost two cousins to the conflict.

Another former fighter, Richard Bende, left in 2019 because he believed the rebellion had become a “scores-settling venture”. He had fought government soldiers in Bamusso, in the Southwest, and now works as a secondary school history and geography teacher. Like Mbah and Mosongo, he avoided the DDR programme, citing concerns about the treatment of former fighters at its centres.

Paul Mukete, who fought in Kumba from 2017 to 2020 under the nickname King of Vultures, chose a different path. But six years after entering the DDR programme in Tiko town, in the Southwest, he says he has little to show for it.

Apart from learning poultry and pig farming, Mukete says he has received no psychological care.

“We gave intelligence information to the military, who used it to kill some separatist fighters who refused to lay down their weapons,” he said. “We were about 600 in the DDR centre, but many have since left out of frustration. Some even rejoined the struggle and got killed.”

The 29-year-old father of three now takes on odd jobs to support his family.

His account raises questions about whether the programme is providing former fighters with the support they need to rebuild their lives and remain out of the conflict.

Fonbeh Hedwick Chia, a mental health specialist and founder of the Bamenda-based Living Vine Mental Health Services, says both fighters and civilians in the English-speaking regions have been exposed to psychological trauma.

He argues that the DDR centres lack the therapeutic support needed to rehabilitate former fighters, estimating that about 800 have renounced the armed struggle.

“The government is more concerned with the propaganda made when they come to the DDR than their integral welfare,” Chia told Al Jazeera, arguing that former fighters need psychological care to address the trauma of atrocities committed and witnessed during the conflict.

Without proper rehabilitation, he warns, former fighters risk remaining marginalised and could become a source of further instability.

The accounts of former fighters and Chia’s assessment point to a central challenge for the DDR programme: persuading rebels to surrender is only the first step, while helping them return to civilian life requires sustained support.

Cameroon’s Anglophone crisis has roots in its colonial past. Initially colonised by Germany in 1884, the territory was divided between Britain and France after World War I.

French Cameroon gained independence in 1960. In 1961, British-administered Southern Cameroons voted in a United Nations-organised plebiscite to join the independent Republic of Cameroon, forming a federal state. The arrangement was dissolved in 1972 following a controversial referendum, ending the Anglophone regions’ federal status.

Unlike some conflicts involving more centralised rebel movements, Cameroon’s separatist rebellion has no single command structure. Dozens of smaller factions operate across Northwest and Southwest, with some receiving financial support and weapons from diaspora groups.

The prolonged fighting has brought human rights abuses by both government forces and separatists. Some armed groups have also shifted towards criminal activities, including kidnapping for ransom.

Chris Roberts, a political scientist at the University of Calgary in Canada, says the conflict is rooted less in language differences than in “decades of poor governance from a political system that has kept the same president in power since 1982”.

Although the government has repeatedly claimed the war is over, Roberts says continued firefights, ambushes and attacks demonstrate otherwise.

He argues that political reform in Yaoundé is essential to ending the conflict. He describes the October 2025 presidential election as “strategically rigged” and argues that it offers little prospect of resolving the crisis. A future presidential succession crisis could create opportunities for reform but also risk destabilising the country.

“There will not be a military solution to this war,” Roberts said.

news.originalContent:
Schumer, who has led the Democratic caucus since 2017, faces a challenge from Chris Van Hollen in his bid to be the next Senate majority leader.

Chuck Schumer, the top Democrat in the United States Senate, is facing backlash against his bid to serve as Senate majority leader in the incoming Congress.

On Sunday, President ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Donald Trump added to the ongoing criticism of Schumer’s leadership, signalling there would be tension with the White House if Schumer were picked again to lead the Democratic caucus.

“It is going to be very hard for me to work with Chuck Schumer should he become Senate Majority ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠Leader,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

“He failed badly as ‘Leader’ once before, one of the worst in history, and I have little doubt that he will fail again.”

The debate over Schumer’s leadership has underscored divides within the Democratic Party, particularly in the wake of the November 3 midterm elections.

Following a historic set of victories, Democrats are set to take control of both chambers of Congress in January.

Schumer, who leads the Democratic Senate minority, is hoping to retain his leadership position. A closed-door, secret-ballot vote is scheduled for December 1 to decide the majority leader.

A senator representing New York since 1999, Schumer has expressed confidence in his odds, saying he has the necessary votes to stay in charge.

“I will be elected majority leader,” Schumer told reporters last week.

But critics say Schumer, who will turn 76 on Monday, is ill-suited to lead a Senate Democratic caucus increasingly shaped by younger, anti-establishment lawmakers.

Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen, backed by progressives, has mounted a campaign to challenge Schumer for the majority leader role.

Van Hollen told NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday that he, too, was confident of winning.

“If you look at our caucus, you can see a huge appetite for change. They are seeing the American people and the Democratic Party calling for change. They also want to change the way we do business in the United States Democratic caucus and the United States Senate,” he said.

Schumer has also seen falling public approval ratings. In mid-November, a poll by the news agency Reuters and the research firm Ipsos found that 34 percent of self-identified Democrats viewed Schumer favourably. That percentage was down from 38 percent in February.

November’s poll also suggested that 43 percent of Democrats held an unfavourable view of Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats since 2017.

The Senate Democratic leader is the only unresolved role among Congress’s top four positions.

House Democrats last week nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be speaker in the next Congress.

Meanwhile, John Thune will continue to lead Senate Republicans, and Representative Jim Jordan ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌will succeed Speaker Mike Johnson as the top House Republican.

news.originalContent:
اجلاس تغییرات اقلیمی سازمان ملل متحد، کاپ ۳۱، در آنتالیای ترکیه دو روز پس از موعد بدون دستیابی به توافق به پایان می‌رسد؛ اتحادیه اروپا و برخی دیگر از طرف‌ها با پیش‌نویس نهایی مخالفت کردند، زیرا که در آن هیچ اشاره‌ای به ضرورت حذف تدریجی سوخت‌های فسیلی، که عامل اصلی گرمایش جهانی هستند، نشده بود.

مراد کوروم، وزیر محیط زیست ترکیه و رئیس اجلاس کاپ ۳۱، اعلام کرد که این توافق‌نامه تصویب نشد؛ موضوعی که به گفته ازمی استالارد، خبرنگار بی‌بی‌سی که در اجلاس آنتالیا حضور دارد، نشان‌دهنده یک تحول تقریبا بی‌سابقه است.

آقای کوروم گفت که پس از ناکامی پیش‌نویس چهارم در دستیابی به توافق میان هیئت‌ها، پیش‌نویس جدیدی برای توافق اقلیمی ارائه نخواهد شد.

کریس بوون، وزیر استرالیایی و یکی از میزبانان مشترک این اجلاس، گفت که برخی طرف‌ها تهدید کردند در صورت گنجاندن موضوع سوخت‌های فسیلی، میز مذاکره را ترک خواهند کرد، در حالی که گروهی دیگر خواستار گنجاندن آن بودند.

آقای بوون گفت که این اجلاس با «پیچیده‌ترین و پرتنش‌ترین فضای ژئوپلیتیک در دوران اخیر» روبرو بوده است.

دارا اوبراین، رئیس هیئت نمایندگی اتحادیه اروپا در این اجلاس، برخی کشورهای نفت‌خیز و تولیدکنندگان سوخت‌های فسیلی را متهم کرد که مذاکرات در ترکیه را «به گروگان گرفتند»؛ زیرا که در چهارمین پیش‌نویس توافق نیز هیچ اشاره‌ای به سوخت‌های فسیلی نشده بود.

برخی کشورهای عربی ابراز داشتند که با حسن نیت همچنان در گفتگوها مشارکت خواهند کرد.

روسیه ضمن دفاع از مخالفت خود با گنجاندن تعهدی برای گذار از سوخت‌های فسیلی، در سخنرانی‌اش مستقیما از اتحادیه اروپا انتقاد کرد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

میاتا فان‌بوله، وزیر انرژی بریتانیا، گفت که عدم موفقیت مذاکرات در «ایجاد اجماع» میان طرفین، «مایوس‌کننده» است.

علاوه بر بریتانیا، کشورهای دیگر هم اعلام کردند که از پیش‌نویس ارائه‌شده در این اجلاس توسط میزبانان مشترک، ترکیه و استرالیا، عمیقا مایوس و سرخورده شده‌اند.

در این پیش‌نویس اذعان شده است که هدف تعیین‌شده در توافق‌نامه پاریس در سال ۲۰۱۵ برای محدود کردن افزایش دمای جهانی به کمتر از ۱/۵ درجه سانتی‌گراد محقق نخواهد شد؛ با فراتر رفتن گرمایش زمین از این مرز، پیامدهای تغییرات اقلیمی به‌طور چشمگیری تشدید خواهند شد.

این اجلاس طولانی‌ترین نشست در تاریخ این مذاکرات محسوب می‌شود، به‌طوری که گفتگوها دو روز پس از زمان مقرر برای پایان آن (جمعه، ۲۰ نوامبر)، همچنان ادامه داشت.

اگر کشورها نتوانند به اجماع برسند، مذاکرات می‌تواند تا سال آینده به حالت تعلیق درآید، امری که پیش‌تر فقط یک بار در اجلاس کاپ رخ داده است.

عدم دستیابی به توافق در این اجلاس در حالی منتشر می‌شود که سایمون استیل، رئیس کنوانسیون چارچوب تغییر اقلیم در سازمان ملل که نهاد سازمان‌دهنده کاپ است، پیش‌تر گفته بود که در مورد «حوزه‌های اصلاح بالقوه» در سیستم «مبتنی بر اجماع» در اجلاس‌های اقلیمی مشاوره خواهد گرفت.

او به خبرنگاران گفت که کاپ ۳۱ «پیشرفت واقعی و نتایج ملموس» داشته است و برخی تصمیمات کلیدی هم، از جمله در مورد برق‌رسانی، گرفته شده است.

آقای استیل در پاسخ به پرسش بی‌بی‌سی که آیا رویکرد مبتنی بر اجماع سازمان ملل هنوز موثر است، گفت: «این فرآیندی است که ما داریم، این فرآیندی است که برای رسیدن ما به این نقطه موثر بوده است. این فرایند کمک کرد اجلاس پاریس را با موفقیت به سرانجام برسانیم... بنابراین می‌تواند موثر باشد.»

آقای استیل اما گفت که این فرآیند امروز «ناکام ماند»؛ او افزود که گفت‌وگو در مورد آن «یک گفت‌وگوی زنده» بود.

این مذاکرات در شرایطی به درازا کشید که کشورها با شوک افزایش قیمت نفت و تنش‌های ژئوپلیتیکی ناشی از جنگ آمریکا و ایران روبه‌رو هستند. خبرگزاری فرانسه می‌گوید که این وضعیت از جمله عواملی است که انتظارات برای دستیابی به پیشرفتی مهم در اجلاس امسال را کاهش داد.

اختلاف اصلی بر سر پیش‌نویس توافق نهایی بوده است. در نسخه اولیه این سند، به تسریع روند کنار گذاشتن سوخت‌های فسیلی اشاره شده بود، اما در نسخه دوم که روز پنجشنبه منتشر شد، تمام اشاره‌ها به نفت و گاز و زغال‌سنگ حذف شد؛ تغییری که با اعتراض شدید شماری از کشورها و تهدید به ترک مذاکرات روبه‌رو شد.

اتحادیه اروپا و کشورهای جزیره‌ای اقیانوس آرام از مخالفان اصلی متن جدید هستند. ووپکه هوکسترا، مسئول مذاکرات اقلیمی اتحادیه اروپا، هشدار داد که «نداشتن توافق بهتر از یک توافق بد است».

وزیر تغییرات اقلیمی ایرلند هم گفت که حدود ۱۳۰ کشور حاضر در اجلاس خواهان آن هستند که در توافق نهایی دست‌کم به سوخت‌های فسیلی و کنار گذاشتن تدریجی آنها اشاره شود.

در مقابل، عربستان سعودی از جمله کشورهایی است که بر سر آینده سوخت‌های فسیلی با اتحادیه اروپا اختلاف دارد.

ریاست اجلاس تلاش کرد که با برگزاری نشست‌هایی میان طرف‌های مخالف، راهی برای دستیابی به توافق پیدا کند.

یکی دیگر از موضوعات اختلاف، پیشنهاد گسترش استفاده از فناوری جذب و ذخیره کربن است؛ فناوری‌ای که صنعت سوخت‌های فسیلی از آن حمایت می‌کند. منتقدان می‌گویند که هزینه بالای این فناوری و عملکرد محدود آن در کاهش انتشار گازهای گلخانه‌ای، ممکن است به ادامه استفاده از سوخت‌های فسیلی منجر شود.

دارا اوبراین، رئیس هیئت نمایندگی اتحادیه اروپا در این اجلاس، برخی کشورهای نفت‌خیز و تولیدکنندگان سوخت‌های فسیلی را متهم کرد که مذاکرات در ترکیه را «به گروگان گرفتند»؛ زیرا که در چهارمین پیش‌نویس توافق نیز هیچ اشاره‌ای به سوخت‌های فسیلی نشده بود.

برخی کشورهای عربی ابراز داشتند که با حسن نیت همچنان در گفتگوها مشارکت خواهند کرد.

روسیه ضمن دفاع از مخالفت خود با گنجاندن تعهدی برای گذار از سوخت‌های فسیلی، در سخنرانی‌اش مستقیما از اتحادیه اروپا انتقاد کرد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

میاتا فان‌بوله، وزیر انرژی بریتانیا، گفت که عدم موفقیت مذاکرات در «ایجاد اجماع» میان طرفین، «مایوس‌کننده» است.

علاوه بر بریتانیا، کشورهای دیگر هم اعلام کردند که از پیش‌نویس ارائه‌شده در این اجلاس توسط میزبانان مشترک، ترکیه و استرالیا، عمیقا مایوس و سرخورده شده‌اند.

در این پیش‌نویس اذعان شده است که هدف تعیین‌شده در توافق‌نامه پاریس در سال ۲۰۱۵ برای محدود کردن افزایش دمای جهانی به کمتر از ۱/۵ درجه سانتی‌گراد محقق نخواهد شد؛ با فراتر رفتن گرمایش زمین از این مرز، پیامدهای تغییرات اقلیمی به‌طور چشمگیری تشدید خواهند شد.

این اجلاس طولانی‌ترین نشست در تاریخ این مذاکرات محسوب می‌شود، به‌طوری که گفتگوها دو روز پس از زمان مقرر برای پایان آن (جمعه، ۲۰ نوامبر)، همچنان ادامه داشت.

اگر کشورها نتوانند به اجماع برسند، مذاکرات می‌تواند تا سال آینده به حالت تعلیق درآید، امری که پیش‌تر فقط یک بار در اجلاس کاپ رخ داده است.

عدم دستیابی به توافق در این اجلاس در حالی منتشر می‌شود که سایمون استیل، رئیس کنوانسیون چارچوب تغییر اقلیم در سازمان ملل که نهاد سازمان‌دهنده کاپ است، پیش‌تر گفته بود که در مورد «حوزه‌های اصلاح بالقوه» در سیستم «مبتنی بر اجماع» در اجلاس‌های اقلیمی مشاوره خواهد گرفت.

او به خبرنگاران گفت که کاپ ۳۱ «پیشرفت واقعی و نتایج ملموس» داشته است و برخی تصمیمات کلیدی هم، از جمله در مورد برق‌رسانی، گرفته شده است.

آقای استیل در پاسخ به پرسش بی‌بی‌سی که آیا رویکرد مبتنی بر اجماع سازمان ملل هنوز موثر است، گفت: «این فرآیندی است که ما داریم، این فرآیندی است که برای رسیدن ما به این نقطه موثر بوده است. این فرایند کمک کرد اجلاس پاریس را با موفقیت به سرانجام برسانیم... بنابراین می‌تواند موثر باشد.»

آقای استیل اما گفت که این فرآیند امروز «ناکام ماند»؛ او افزود که گفت‌وگو در مورد آن «یک گفت‌وگوی زنده» بود.

این مذاکرات در شرایطی به درازا کشید که کشورها با شوک افزایش قیمت نفت و تنش‌های ژئوپلیتیکی ناشی از جنگ آمریکا و ایران روبه‌رو هستند. خبرگزاری فرانسه می‌گوید که این وضعیت از جمله عواملی است که انتظارات برای دستیابی به پیشرفتی مهم در اجلاس امسال را کاهش داد.

اختلاف اصلی بر سر پیش‌نویس توافق نهایی بوده است. در نسخه اولیه این سند، به تسریع روند کنار گذاشتن سوخت‌های فسیلی اشاره شده بود، اما در نسخه دوم که روز پنجشنبه منتشر شد، تمام اشاره‌ها به نفت و گاز و زغال‌سنگ حذف شد؛ تغییری که با اعتراض شدید شماری از کشورها و تهدید به ترک مذاکرات روبه‌رو شد.

اتحادیه اروپا و کشورهای جزیره‌ای اقیانوس آرام از مخالفان اصلی متن جدید هستند. ووپکه هوکسترا، مسئول مذاکرات اقلیمی اتحادیه اروپا، هشدار داد که «نداشتن توافق بهتر از یک توافق بد است».

وزیر تغییرات اقلیمی ایرلند هم گفت که حدود ۱۳۰ کشور حاضر در اجلاس خواهان آن هستند که در توافق نهایی دست‌کم به سوخت‌های فسیلی و کنار گذاشتن تدریجی آنها اشاره شود.

در مقابل، عربستان سعودی از جمله کشورهایی است که بر سر آینده سوخت‌های فسیلی با اتحادیه اروپا اختلاف دارد.

ریاست اجلاس تلاش کرد که با برگزاری نشست‌هایی میان طرف‌های مخالف، راهی برای دستیابی به توافق پیدا کند.

یکی دیگر از موضوعات اختلاف، پیشنهاد گسترش استفاده از فناوری جذب و ذخیره کربن است؛ فناوری‌ای که صنعت سوخت‌های فسیلی از آن حمایت می‌کند. منتقدان می‌گویند که هزینه بالای این فناوری و عملکرد محدود آن در کاهش انتشار گازهای گلخانه‌ای، ممکن است به ادامه استفاده از سوخت‌های فسیلی منجر شود.

news.originalContent:
با آغاز فصل سرما در ایران، خاموشی‌های برنامه‌ریزی‌شده برق بار دیگر به خانه‌ها و کسب‌وکارها بازگشته است. شرکت توانیر اعلام کرده است که از امروز، یکشنبه اول آذر، به دلیل محدودیت در تامین سوخت نیروگاه‌ها، قطع برنامه‌ریزی‌شده برق در بخش‌های خانگی و تجاری از سر گرفته می‌شود.

توانیر هدف از اعمال این محدودیت‌ها را مدیریت منابع موجود و حفظ پایداری شبکه برق کشور اعلام کرده است.

محمد اله‌داد، ، مدیرعامل شرکت توانیر، با اشاره به کمبود سوخت نیروگاه‌ها به‌عنوان علت اجرای محدودیت‌های تازه، گفته است که خاموشی‌ها ممکن است به شکل «دو ساعت قطعی برق در دو روز یا حداکثر دو ساعت در هر روز» اعمال شود.

او در عین حال تاکید کرده است که زمان اجرای خاموشی‌ها ثابت نیست و برنامه قطع برق با توجه به «شرایط شبکه و نحوه  مدیریت محدودیت‌ها» تغییر خواهد کرد.

تداوم خاموشی‌ها علاوه بر اختلال در زندگی روزمره خانوارها، مشکلاتی برای کسب‌وکارها و واحدهای تولیدی نیز ایجاد می‌کند. قطع برق می‌تواند فعالیت مغازه‌ها، کارگاه‌ها و کارخانه‌ها را مختل کند و در مواردی به توقف خطوط تولید، خسارت به مواد اولیه و تجهیزات و کاهش درآمد صاحبان مشاغل منجر شود.

بازگشت خاموشی‌ها در حالی است که برنامه قطع برق که در ماه‌های گرم سال اجرا می‌شد، برای مدتی متوقف شده بود. عباس علی‌آبادی، وزیر نیرو، نیز در شهریورماه از بهبود وضعیت شبکه برق خبر داده و گفته بود: «زمستان سختی در پیش نخواهد بود و برنامه‌ای برای قطع برق برنامه‌ریزی‌شده وجود ندارد.»

با این حال، بازگشت محدودیت‌ها در آغاز فصل سرما نشان می‌دهد که مشکلات تامین انرژی در ایران با پایان فصل گرما برطرف نشده است. در حالی که افزایش مصرف برق در تابستان عمدتا به استفاده از وسایل سرمایشی مربوط می‌شود، در زمستان افزایش مصرف گاز برای گرمایش، تامین سوخت نیروگاه‌ها را با دشواری بیشتری روبه‌رو می‌کند.

دولت می‌گوید کمبود سوخت باعث شده که برق تولیدی نیروگاه‌ها کفاف تقاضا را ندهد و می‌خواهد با خاموش کردن خانه‌ها و مغازه‌ها، چراغ کارخانه‌ها را روشن نگه دارد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس‌جمهور ایران، نیز در ماه‌های اخیر بارها از مردم خواسته است برای مدیریت بحران انرژی، مصرف برق و گاز را کاهش دهند.

او با تاکید بر اهمیت مدیریت مصرف در شرایط جنگی، از مردم خواسته است دمای خانه‌های خود را چند درجه کاهش دهند و با پوشیدن لباس گرم‌تر، مصرف وسایل گرمایشی را کنترل کنند.

آقای پزشکیان همچنین با اشاره به میزان بالای مصرف انرژی در ایران گفته است که کشور «حدود سه برابر میانگین جهانی» انرژی مصرف می‌کند و تاکید کرده است که حتی بدون وقوع جنگ نیز، ادامه روند کنونی مصرف می‌تواند مشکلات جدی در تامین برق و گاز ایجاد کند.

به گفته رئیس‌جمهور ایران، این کشور در گذشته نیز در دوره اوج مصرف با «ناترازی روزانه ۲۵۰ تا ۳۰۰ میلیون مترمکعب گاز» مواجه بوده است.

صداوسیمای ایران نیز جمعه شب گزارشی را منتشر کرد که نشان می‌دهد، مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس‌جمهور این کشور، در یک اتاق تاریک و بدون مرکز گرمی و در هوای سرد کار می‌کند.

ویدیو نشان می‌دهد بسیاری از چراغ‌ها خاموش است و مسعود پزشکیان در دفترش با کاپشن نشسته و دما از ۲۰ درجه کمتر است. پخش این ویدیو با واکنش هم همراه بوده است.

به گفته خبرنگاران در غیاب ابزارهای قیمتی، به نظر می‌رسد که دولت آقای پزشکیان می‌خواهد با چنین ویدیوهایی مردم را قانع به صرفه‌جویی کند. ولی منتقدان به تندی از دولت انتقاد کرده‌اند. روزنامه اصولگرای کیهان در پستی در صفحه تلگرامش نوشت که «این تصویر حتی از ضعیف‌ترین ممالک آفریقا هم دیده نمی‌شود» و مسعود پزشکیان را متهم کرده است که «چوب حراج به عزت مردم ایران زده» است.

اما به گفته تحلیلگران واقعیت این است که کمبود حامل‌های انرژی از جمله برق و گاز طبیعی حاصل سال‌ها و دهه‌ها سرمایه‌گذاری ناکافی در تولید و شکست در مدیریت مصرف است و نتیجه‌اش این که نه تابستان برق هست و حالا دیگر نه زمستان.

در کنار مشکلات ساختاری صنعت انرژی،  مقام‌های جمهوری اسلامی حملات آمریکا و اسرائیل به زیرساخت‌های انرژی ایران را نیز از عوامل تشدیدکننده بحران کنونی می‌دانند. در جریان این حملات به تاسیسات منطقه ویژه اقتصادی انرژی پارس در عسلویه، بخش‌هایی از زیرساخت‌های گاز آسیب دید و تعدادی از واحدها از مدار تولید خارج شدند.

به گفته مقام‌های ایرانی، آسیب به این تاسیسات در کنار ناترازی پیشین انرژی، تامین سوخت نیروگاه‌ها و تولید برق را دشوارتر کرده است واکنون با آغاز فصل سرما، کمبود سوخت نیروگاه‌ها بار دیگر به اعمال محدودیت در تامین برق منجر شده است. این وضعیت بار دیگر مسئله ناترازی انرژی و توان دولت برای تامین پایدار برق و گاز در ماه‌های سرد سال را در کانون توجه قرار داده است.

دولت می‌گوید کمبود سوخت باعث شده که برق تولیدی نیروگاه‌ها کفاف تقاضا را ندهد و می‌خواهد با خاموش کردن خانه‌ها و مغازه‌ها، چراغ کارخانه‌ها را روشن نگه دارد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس‌جمهور ایران، نیز در ماه‌های اخیر بارها از مردم خواسته است برای مدیریت بحران انرژی، مصرف برق و گاز را کاهش دهند.

او با تاکید بر اهمیت مدیریت مصرف در شرایط جنگی، از مردم خواسته است دمای خانه‌های خود را چند درجه کاهش دهند و با پوشیدن لباس گرم‌تر، مصرف وسایل گرمایشی را کنترل کنند.

آقای پزشکیان همچنین با اشاره به میزان بالای مصرف انرژی در ایران گفته است که کشور «حدود سه برابر میانگین جهانی» انرژی مصرف می‌کند و تاکید کرده است که حتی بدون وقوع جنگ نیز، ادامه روند کنونی مصرف می‌تواند مشکلات جدی در تامین برق و گاز ایجاد کند.

به گفته رئیس‌جمهور ایران، این کشور در گذشته نیز در دوره اوج مصرف با «ناترازی روزانه ۲۵۰ تا ۳۰۰ میلیون مترمکعب گاز» مواجه بوده است.

صداوسیمای ایران نیز جمعه شب گزارشی را منتشر کرد که نشان می‌دهد، مسعود پزشکیان، رئیس‌جمهور این کشور، در یک اتاق تاریک و بدون مرکز گرمی و در هوای سرد کار می‌کند.

ویدیو نشان می‌دهد بسیاری از چراغ‌ها خاموش است و مسعود پزشکیان در دفترش با کاپشن نشسته و دما از ۲۰ درجه کمتر است. پخش این ویدیو با واکنش هم همراه بوده است.

به گفته خبرنگاران در غیاب ابزارهای قیمتی، به نظر می‌رسد که دولت آقای پزشکیان می‌خواهد با چنین ویدیوهایی مردم را قانع به صرفه‌جویی کند. ولی منتقدان به تندی از دولت انتقاد کرده‌اند. روزنامه اصولگرای کیهان در پستی در صفحه تلگرامش نوشت که «این تصویر حتی از ضعیف‌ترین ممالک آفریقا هم دیده نمی‌شود» و مسعود پزشکیان را متهم کرده است که «چوب حراج به عزت مردم ایران زده» است.

اما به گفته تحلیلگران واقعیت این است که کمبود حامل‌های انرژی از جمله برق و گاز طبیعی حاصل سال‌ها و دهه‌ها سرمایه‌گذاری ناکافی در تولید و شکست در مدیریت مصرف است و نتیجه‌اش این که نه تابستان برق هست و حالا دیگر نه زمستان.

در کنار مشکلات ساختاری صنعت انرژی،  مقام‌های جمهوری اسلامی حملات آمریکا و اسرائیل به زیرساخت‌های انرژی ایران را نیز از عوامل تشدیدکننده بحران کنونی می‌دانند. در جریان این حملات به تاسیسات منطقه ویژه اقتصادی انرژی پارس در عسلویه، بخش‌هایی از زیرساخت‌های گاز آسیب دید و تعدادی از واحدها از مدار تولید خارج شدند.

به گفته مقام‌های ایرانی، آسیب به این تاسیسات در کنار ناترازی پیشین انرژی، تامین سوخت نیروگاه‌ها و تولید برق را دشوارتر کرده است واکنون با آغاز فصل سرما، کمبود سوخت نیروگاه‌ها بار دیگر به اعمال محدودیت در تامین برق منجر شده است. این وضعیت بار دیگر مسئله ناترازی انرژی و توان دولت برای تامین پایدار برق و گاز در ماه‌های سرد سال را در کانون توجه قرار داده است.

منبع تصویر، Instagram/_sadafhaghbin_

هادی نیرومند، دادستان عمومی و انقلاب شهرستان خمام، می‌گوید فرد متهم به قتل صدف حق‌بین «به ارتکاب قتل اقرار کرده» و «تحقیقات قضایی درباره ابعاد مختلف این حادثه» همچنان ادامه دارد.

به گفته او «در جریان تحقیقات مقدماتی، بررسی‌های اولیه حاکی از آن است که متهم در ساعات پایانی شب حادثه، حدود ساعت ۲۱:۳۰، به دنبال مقتول رفته و سپس به اتفاق یکدیگر در مراسم جشن تولد یکی از دوستان حضور پیدا کرده‌اند.»

به گفته این مقام قضایی در جشن تولد «میان طرفین اختلاف و مشاجره لفظی شکل می‌گیرد» و متهم به ظن داشتن رابطه دوستی میان مقتول و شخص دیگری «از مقتول خواسته بود با آن شخص ثالث تماس گرفته و او را به محل مهمانی دعوت کند که با مخالفت مقتول مواجه شده است. متعاقب این اتفاق، متهم با استفاده از یک قبضه سلاح شکاری فاقد مجوز قانونی، به سمت مقتول تیراندازی کرده و این اقدام منجر به فوت وی شده است.»

به گفته آقای نیرومند «متهم در جریان تحقیقات مقدماتی به ارتکاب قتل اقرار کرده» و «تحقیقات قضایی با هدف روشن شدن تمامی ابعاد حادثه، بررسی انگیزه احتمالی ارتکاب جرم، نحوه تهیه و نگهداری سلاح و مهمات و سایر موضوعات مرتبط همچنان ادامه دارد.»

پیش از این یک منبع مطلع به بی‌بی‌سی فارسی گفته بود که متهم که دوست‌پسر سابق صدف بود، مهمانان را در اتاقی حبس کرد و صدف را به اتاقی دیگر برد. صدف در حالی که از دیگران کمک می‌خواست، هدف گلوله قرار گرفت.

به گفته این منبع آگاه، متهم ۲۹ ساله، سابقه آزار روحی و جسمی صدف را داشته و به همین دلیل رابطه آنها چند ماه بیشتر دوام نیاورده است. شبی که قتل صورت گرفته هم صدف در ابتدا تمایلی به بیرون رفتن از خانه نداشته، اما پس از دریافت پیامی که او را آشفته کرده، گفته است که مجبور است برود.

به گفته این منبع، خانواده صدف به تلفن همراه او دسترسی ندارند تا پیام‌های ردوبدل‌شده پیش از حادثه را بررسی کنند و این تلفن در اختیار پلیس است.

این منبع گفت متهم هنگام فرار، تصادف کرد که به مجروح شدن یک نفر انجامید و پلیس او را هنگام فرار از صحنه تصادف بازداشت کرده است.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

سرهنگ ایمان جهان‌دیده، فرمانده انتظامی خمام پس از وقوع این حادثه گفته بود که ماموران پس از دریافت گزارش تیراندازی مرگبار به محل اعزام شدند و«بررسی‌های اولیه نشان داد فردی به دلیل اختلافات شخصی با استفاده از یک قبضه اسلحه شکاری به سوی زنی شلیک کرده و پس از آن از محل گریخته است.»

فرمانده انتظامی شهرستان خمام گفته بود مرد متهم به قتل در کمتر از چند ساعت بازداشت شده است.

پس از انتشار خبر قتل صدف حق‌بین، مطالبی درباره آخرین فعالیت‌های او در شبکه‌های اجتماعی نیز بازنشر شده است.

بر اساس تصاویر منتشرشده از حساب اینستاگرام او، صدف دو شب پیش از مرگش مطلبی در سوگ سوگند صیادی منتشر کرده بود.

در استوری که صدف منتشر کرده بود این جمله نوشته شده است: «به دختراتون یاد بدید وقتی یه مرد روشون دست بلند کرد نابودش کنن. چون شما می‌تونید اون رو از زندان دربیارید اما از قبر نه!»

سوگند صیادی، دختر ۱۶ ساله، اخیرا در کرمانشاه به قتل رسید و پدرش در همین ارتباط بازداشت شد.

قتل صدف حق‌بین و سوگند صیادی در حالی رخ داده است که اخیرا، موضوع کشته‌شدن زنان به دست همسران، شرکای عاطفی، اعضای خانواده یا در اماکن عمومی بار دیگر در مرکز توجه قرار گرفته است.

A voter group renewed its push for open primaries in the Big Apple, filing a petition with 75,000 signatures despite ongoing legal battles with City Hall and opposition from Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Nonpartisan political group Unite NY delivered the signatures to the City Clerk’s Office to replace 42,000 signatures it delivered in July that the city claimed were illegitimate — thereby thwarting the group’s efforts to get the open primary measure on the ballot, according to a press release.

The new petitions were aimed to restart the process to get the open primary ballot initiative before voters ahead of the next mayor’s election in 2029 and work around the ongoing lawsuit against the city about the July petitions — which the city claimed contained invalid signatures.

Democrats outnumber Republicans 6-to-1 in the city — which usually means the outcome of Election Day is decided solely by registered Democrats months before — with more than a million unaffiliated voters left essentially disenfranchised, according to critics.

“More than 110,000 New Yorkers have signed petitions because they believe every voter deserves a voice in our elections,” said Anthony Thomas, executive director of Unite NY.

Mamdani, who notched a dark horse upset in the 2025 Democratic primary before fending off a November challenge from Democrat Andrew Cuomo on an independent line, has defended closed primaries as City Hall continued to stymie the ballot initiative.

Unite NY was working towards collecting 15,000 more signatures — which if accepted, would render its current legal battle over the July signatures moot.

Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was ejected from their loss to the Eagles on Sunday following a pair of unsportsmanlike penalties, marking his second time being tossed from a game in the last two seasons.

The second penalty occurred following an incomplete pass from Aaron Rodgers to Germie Bernard in the end zone, when Metcalf and Marcus Epps got into a skirmish near the area as a group of players gathered around.

DK Metcalf has been ejected for unsportsmanlike conduct.Metcalf was ejected after two personal fouls.(📺 CBS) pic.twitter.com/f1OE50Fn6I

“He’s done nothing statistically but continues to get in these brawls,” CBS play-by-play broadcaster Kevin Harlan said.

CBS broadcast cameras also captured Metcalf putting his hand near Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean’s face mask, too.

Metcalf also drew an unnecessary roughness penalty in the first half after a skirmish with DeJean.

It marked the third time in his career that Metcalf has been ejected, according to ESPN — tied for the most across that stretch with 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw.

Metcalf had collected just one catch for two yards during Sunday’s game, and he entered with just 432 receiving yards and a pair of touchdowns this season.

Sharlize True Trujillo was crowned Miss California 2026 in June. But it took a video of her dancing during a UCLA Bruins football game going viral for her to reach celebrity status.

The post showed a side profile of her during a UCLA game and was captioned, “game day let’s bring it home all the way ucla”.

Dollinger commented on the post, writing, “that’s my girl”.

“hi love,” Trujillo wrote back.

All of Trujillo’s social media posts get a lot of comments, especially since that aforementioned video went viral.

Many people are hoping that she becomes a Los Angeles Rams cheerleader in the future, given that she is a senior at UCLA right now.

Regardless of what Trujillo’s future holds, she has already cultivated quite the fan base that she can capitalize on.

news.originalContent:

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries on Sunday refused to rule out trying to impeach members of President Trump’s administration when Democrats take control of Congress in January.

“We haven’t ruled anything in, and we haven’t ruled anything out,” the New York City pol told CBS’ Margaret Brennan on “Face the Nation” when asked whether impeachments would be an immediate priority for House Dems.

Jeffries, who is expected to become House speaker when the new Congress convenes, only said the Democrats would prioritize lowering costs for Americans while holding the Trump administration accountable for what he described as unprecedented corruption.

“We’ve promised the American people that, in addition to our affordability agenda, we know, in the face of the unprecedented corruption that has been unleashed on the American people and the country over the last two years, that we need to deal with accountability,” Jeffries said.

He said the Dems would investigate anyone accused of “stealing from the American people, screwing over the American people or shortchanging the American people.

“We will also hold the crooks accountable,” he said.

Jeffries added that any investigations would be guided by the evidence and the law.

“My expectation is that with respect to the accountability agenda that everyone involved and whatever investigations are unveiled, they’re going to follow the facts, they’re going to apply the law, they’re going to be guided by the Constitution, and they’re going to let the chips fall where they may,” he said.

Jeffries also outlined several priorities for Democrats when they take control of the House, including reversing Medicaid cuts, restoring some slashed food-stamp benefits, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits and addressing the rising costs associated with Trump’s tariffs.

Democrats will rule the House with 257 members compared to 172 GOPers come January.

Hakeem also called for an end to the war with Iran, which he blamed for driving up gas, food and diesel prices.

The incoming speaker said Democrats would seek to ban members of Congress from trading individual stocks early in the new session, too, describing the move as part of the party’s broader accountability agenda.

Democrats’ return to power will give them greater investigative authority and subpoena power to scrutinize the Trump administration, setting up a potential clash with the White House.

The Dems also will take control of the Senate by 56 to 44 starting next year.

Trump was impeached twice during his first term, in 2019 and 2021 under Democratic control of the House, though the Senate acquitted him both times, with Republicans outnumbering the Dems in 2019 but not in 2021.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

San Francisco could experience catastrophic flooding during Thanksgiving as record king tides continue to head its way.

A new visualization from UC Santa Cruz shows how San Francisco’s waterfront and bay communities could be overcome by rising sea levels, leading up to monster king tides.

Just to be clear, what the imagery shows is a hypothetical possibility. It hasn’t happened and it can’t be taken as an official forecast.

“This video depicts a potential El Niño event in San Francisco’s North Bay during winter ‘26/’27,” the video produced by UCSC reads.

“We assume a 20-year storm event with 20 inches (~50 cm) of sea level above normal. Flood levels are based on modeling by the USGS and available on Our Coast Our Future (www.ourcoastourfuture.org).”

The video also says: “In past El Niños, sea levels typically run 6-12” higher than average years. Tide gauges across San Francisco Bay are already running 14’’ above normal for the past 30 days (Oct. 17- Nov. 16) and are rising. Flooding is derived from hydrodynamic modeling results, the wave surface uses a physics-informed visual approximation.”

This comes after a great amount of rainfall in San Francisco earlier in the week that overpowered its drainage capacity and inundated its streets.

With these conditions expected to continue, one place that could suffer the effects of king tides is the Bay Area’s largest airport: San Francisco International Airport. That’s according to what National Weather Service meteorologist Dylan Flynn told the San Francisco Chronicle Saturday.

San Francisco Bay water is expected to surge about 10 feet, flooding the airport, which has seawalls in vulnerable spots only 8 feet high, according to Flynn.

The seawater will reach the airport over three straight days, Flynn added.

Flynn said he sent a message to the airport’s emergency manager on Saturday to alert him of the flooding that’s expected.

Fraser Shilling, director of the UC Davis Road Ecology Center, told the Chronicle that the airport’s pumps would probably not be able to manage such conditions.

“No single runway will escape if it goes over the top,” said Shilling.

The scientist has published a study previously that looks into the risks of flooding at SFO and the Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport.

He’s also looked into low-lying transportation areas in California.

SFO spokesperson Doug Yakel, however, has said the airport will be able to handle the flooding and keep the airport operational.

He added that the airport will be able to protect its tarmac with vinyl sheet pile walls, concrete seawalls and concrete-capped earthen berms it’s equipped with.

“SFO facilities staff are also taking steps to further reduce flooding risk by clearing drainage areas, ensuring pump stations are in top condition, and preparing sand bags and flood barriers if needed,” Yakel said.

Bay Area residents have been warned to avoid unneeded travel Tuesday and Wednesday, and in some cases Monday and Thursday too.

The enormous tides, in addition to the storms, will lead to flooding in near ground areas, affecting freeways and other transportation.

The fact that it’s all coming during the holiday break will likely lead to dangerous situations at a time when travel before Thanksgiving is expected to peak.

Flynn, however, has said that it remains unclear whether the flooding will affect runways or taxiways at SFO.

news.originalContent:
Parties remain split on who will lead the next government and whether far right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir will join.

Talks between the parties of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government have ended without a deal.

Representatives of Netanyahu’s Likud and Eisenkot’s Yashar parties met in a Herzliya hotel on Sunday, where they remained split on who would lead the next government and whether far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir would be part of it, according to Israel’s Channel 12 broadcaster.

The Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper reported that Likud wanted Ben-Gvir in government, while Yashar insisted on his exclusion.

In a joint statement, the two parties said they had “outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues” and that a “follow-up meeting would be held”, without revealing a date or any further details.

Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after the elections in October gave his bloc 48 seats – 13 short of a majority.

Netanyahu has called for a unity government, saying it was the only way that Israel’s security could be guaranteed. Such an arrangement would allow a government to be formed without the inclusion of parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats.

Channel 12 reported that former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together list, proposed a coalition of Together, Yashar, Likud and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beiteinu, with Eisenkot serving first and Netanyahu succeeding him.

However, Eisenkot has opposed a rotation, and Netanyahu has reportedly insisted on taking the premiership first, while Lieberman has ruled out joining any government that includes Netanyahu altogether.

If unity talks fail, Yashar plans to seek a confidence vote in the Knesset for a minority government before Eisenkot’s mandate expires. It would rely on outside support from the Arab Joint List, led by Yousef Jabareen, and the United Arab List, led by Mansour Abbas.

A 10-year-old girl was hospitalized Sunday after getting smashed in the head with a stick by a 67-year-old homeless nut she bumped into at a Queens subway station, police and sources said.

Cops and sources said the unidentified child was at the 7 train platform at the 33rd Street and Boston Street station shortly before 12:30 p.m. when the encounter unfolded.

Police responded to the scene on a 911 call, and found the youngster complaining about her head hurting, and was taken to New York Presbyterian Queens Hospital in stable condition.

Her alleged attacker, who has not been officially charged, was taken into custody.

Law enforcement sources said the creep has three prior arrests, most recently a 2013 bust for allegedly repeatedly punching a 68-year-old man in the face during a dispute.

In that case, the victim told cops he was sitting on a bench at the High Street station at Red Cross Place and Cadman Plaza East when he was attacked.

news.originalContent:
KC Current win NWSL championship as Spirit lose third consecutive final despite playing in front of rowdy home crowd.

Washington, DC – Trinity Rodman sat on the pitch and held her face in her hands, trying to hold back tears as the final whistle ended her Washington Spirit’s quest for the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) with a 2-1 loss to the Kansas City Current.

For Rodman, who could be seen wincing in pain throughout the match after an early shoulder injury, the loss in the final on Saturday night was a familiar feeling. She and the Spirit had reached, but lost, the two previous finals.

This one, however, was different. The Spirit were playing in front of their home fans – a sold-out crowd at Audi Field in Washington, DC, and palpable support across the city.

The third time was not the charm for the Spirit.

The stakes were high on Saturday night with a huge turnout at the stadium and increased interest in women’s football across the country. Former footballer Tobin Heath compared the NWSL to the National Football League (NFL), the most-watched sports league in the US.

And with their cult-like following, the Spirit were hoping to leave local fans with a memory of sporting glory that would last a lifetime.

“The ladies fought hard. I don’t think it was the best performance, but they fought hard. They fought to the end. They were still in it in the 90-something minute, but I wish they would have won,” Spirit fan Angel Ughiovhe told Al Jazeera.

After the KC Current went 2-0 up, Rodman had clawed a goal back in the dying moments of the match, cutting the deficit in half, giving fans a glimmer of hope for a historic comeback that never materialised.

“We were saying internally, third time is a charm,” Kim Bolt, chief marketing and strategy officer at the Washington Spirit, told Al Jazeera on Friday.

“I think especially because our fans mean so much to us, it would just be absolutely incredible if we could get the win in front of our, you know, rowdy Audi crowd.”

That belief was shared across the city. But it just wasn’t meant to be.

Despite the defeat, the final highlighted the passion for women’s football in the US capital and the adoration for the local team.

The soaring arches of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Bridge glowed with the team’s green and pink colours ahead of the final. People across the city walked around with the team’s top that features Washington’s famous cherry blossom. Even the public buses said, “Go Spirit!”

For many Spirit fans, the final was more than a game. Chants of “Free DC” rang out in the stadium at the end of the 51st minute as they have for the past year since President Donald Trump deployed federal troops in the city.

The chant, which is timed to reflect DC’s quest to become the 51st US state, was echoed by spectators outside the stadium at nearby watch parties, highlighting the popularity of the political culture that fans had built around the team.

The capital city is home to nearly 700,000 people who do not have voting members in Congress because DC is not a state.

Carlene Reid said she was disappointed by the outcome of the match on Saturday but she took solace in that people across the country heard the demand for DC statehood.

“This is probably the most inclusive game I’ve ever come to and the most politically sound game,” Reid told Al Jazeera.

“It was absolutely amazing to hear the chant happen as a DC resident. So I’m happy that the message is getting out there that we are fighting for statehood.”

KC Current midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly from a corner in the 54th minute on Saturday shortly after the stadium erupted with the politically charged chant. Brazilian legend Debinha added a second for the champions from a counterattack in the 97th minute.

Rodman scored from a header minutes later.

The win cements Kansas City’s status as a football hub for the men’s and women’s games. Despite its relatively small population of 520,000 people, the city also has a team in the country’s top men’s football league, Major League Soccer (MLS), and it hosted six FIFA World Cup matches over the summer.

Football has been growing in popularity in the US, especially after Argentinian legend Lionel Messi joined Inter Miami in 2023. Cohosting the World Cup with Canada and Mexico only accelerated that trend. The US also hosted the Club World Cup in 2025.

Bolt said the surging interest in men’s football has not come at the expense of the women’s game.

“We have our own fan base that is passionate, that is hungry for content, that is hungry for our merch, hungry for our ticket sales,” Bolt told Al Jazeera.

“The growth in the men’s game – we’re not seeing that cannibalise or stunt our own growth because I think the fan bases are pretty unique.”

Attendance at Spirit’s home games at Audi Field – a 20,000-seat stadium – backs that theory. The Spirit played in front of sold-out crowds in the quarterfinal and semifinal.

And there wasn’t an empty seat on Saturday night despite the skyrocketing ticket prices, which started at more than $300 on the resale market.

The Spirit partnered with DC Mayor-elect Janeese Lewis George to give away 400 tickets through a raffle.

Audi Field on Saturday featured some of the top players in the game between the two squads, who could play key roles for their national teams at the Women’s World Cup in Brazil next year.

On the Current side, Croix Bethune and Michelle Cooper are likely to feature for the US Women’s National Team (USWNT). Temwa Chawinga, who led Malawi to the Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) final earlier this year, is expected to lead her country at the World Cup.

For the Spirit, Rodman was a young, rising star at the last tournament, but she heads into next year as one of the most renowned players in the sport as the USWNT push to reclaim the title from Spain.

The Spirit’s number 10, Leicy Santos, is also set to shine on the international stage with Colombia, while defender Esme Morgan is likely to be called up for England. Sandy MacIver is expected to start between the sticks for Scotland.

Algeria’s Melissa Bethi could also feature at the tournament after her team secured qualification by reaching the WAFCON semifinals.

“One of the best things about DC is that it is an international city,” Bolt said.

“We love the fact that our team is a reflection of the city, the diversity of the city – that we have so many international players.”

It’s on-the-record reptile denial.

A New York state politician clapped back at cold-blooded crazies who launched a conspiracy theory that he’s a reptile after a bizarre clip of his eyes circulated on social media.

The reptile accusations swirled after conspiracy sleuths captured Jordan Wright, a Democratic Assemblyman for New York’s 70th District in Harlem, standing in the crowd during a City Hall press conference about a plan to shut down Rikers Island on Friday.

Wright, 32, appeared to flash a small grin before blinking and rolling his eyes in the back of his head as Mayor Zohran Mamdani spoke to reporters.

“This is how lizards blink … I am pretty sure there is full-blown ‘Men in Black’ aliens walking among us disguised as human beings, and they are hiding in plain sight,” one conspiracy theorist said in a video of Wright on social media.

Wright scaled back the speculation in a statement to The Post, assuring that his work as a lawmaker shows he’s “obviously” human.

“I have no idea what was going on in that video. I’m really not sure,” Wright admitted.

“Obviously I’m a human being, and my humanity can be seen through my legislation like the $4 million for the WE ACT environmental justice center in Harlem,” he said. “I can’t speak to any reptiles or aliens.”

Wright, the son of Manhattan Democratic Party chairman Keith LT Wright, championed the $4 million allocation of funds from the state’s capital projects budget for the center, which is under construction in West Harlem.

The incumbent assemblyman won his reelection campaign to represent District 70 in November. The district covers Manhattanville, part of Hamilton Heights, and most of Central Harlem.

Wright ran uncontested in the general election after beating democratic socialist Conrad Blackburn in the Democratic Party primary in June.

news.originalContent:
United suffer their worst result under a new manager in 100 years as Liverpool cruise past Mauricio Pochettino’s side.

If Mauricio Pochettino had any doubt about the size of the job in front of him at Manchester United, his players confirmed his worst fears within 13 minutes of his first game in charge – a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

As the home side surged into a two-goal lead in the opening exchanges at Anfield, with the away side reduced to 10 men, the sinking sensation for United – who are second bottom of the Premier League – immediately returned.

Any ‘new-manager bounce’, as feared by Reds manager Andoni Iraola, had no time to materialise with a rash challenge from Lenny Yoro on Alexander Isak leading to a straight red in the eighth minute.

The resulting free-kick was powered home by Dominik Szoboszlai, with Florian Wirtz thereafter converting a sharp attack in a flash – ending the match as a contest.

Pochettino slammed the decision to send off Yoro after the game, but there was a familiar feeling about the performance overall.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at five key takeaways as the opening salvo of the ninth manager since United’s last league title in 2013 fell apart – resulting in the worst start for a new manager of the club in 100 years.

Even though United have greater concerns, the answer was undoubtedly: no. The question for the referee, in sending off Yoro for denying a goalscoring opportunity, had four considerations: distance between the offence and the goal, general direction of the play, likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball, and location and number of defenders.

Of those guidelines, the most pertinent were the direction of play, which was at an angle across the box, and the likelihood of keeping control of the ball – Isak arguably had no control of it at all after a heavy first touch that allowed United keeper Senne Lammens to gather.

VAR (video assistant referee) had the chance to ask the referee to reconsider his decision, but decided there was no clear and obvious error. Had the referee reviewed the red card, then he would have surely decided a yellow card would have sufficed.

The play that led to the card being shown, however, was even more questionable than the outcome.

The release of the team sheets, an hour and 15 minutes before kickoff, was the first moment all United fans looked to.

For all the pre-game comments by Pochettino, the Argentinean’s starting 11 was always going to be the first true sense of his evaluation of United’s current woes.

Dropping defender Harry Maguire, a former club captain, was a massive call – all the more so given the inexperience of Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt, who were both selected ahead of the ex-England stalwart.

The ref’s mistake in sending off Yoro was clear, but Yoro and de Ligt were heavily exposed in the play that led to the sending-off.

The latter is easing his way back into first-team action after a year out with a back injury and found himself in no-man’s land as Isak chased a long ball. Yoro sought to cover, but was clumsy and ill-advised in his attempt, allowing Isak to draw what was only a soft challenge and connection.

United were plucky after the change forced by the sending-off, with Maguire replacing the clearly, and understandably, disappointed Bryan Mbeumo.

Maguire’s fine, last-ditch block from Isak’s close-range pivot and shot saved United’s blushes five minutes before the break, and made Pochettino’s first big call look all the worse.

A scuffed attempt at a clearance early in the second half by de Ligt allowed Isak clean through only for the Liverpool forward to slice his effort.

By the time Rio Ngumoha added a 66th-minute third, all the questions about a defence that had previously shipped 30 goals in 15 games this season had been answered. The fourth from Victor Munoz was inevitable, and it could have been a lot worse for United on the day.

Should Pochettino not find some considerable longer-term strategies soon, then the desperate may well turn to the unimaginable.

The heat is turning up for the Red Devils, and the patience of the fans has already run thin with the players this season.

The much-maligned ownership of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos group can also expect prolonged protests, as seen of late.

Change in the dugout appears as though it will not be anywhere near enough to reverse a trend 13 years in the making – and the fans’ unswerving support of Pochettino’s predecessor, Michael Carrick, attests to the fact that wholesale reformation is warranted.

If Mauricio Pochettino had any doubt about the size of the job in front of him at Manchester United, his players confirmed his worst fears within 13 minutes of his first game in charge – a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

As the home side surged into a two-goal lead in the opening exchanges at Anfield, with the away side reduced to 10 men, the sinking sensation for United – who are second bottom of the Premier League – immediately returned.

Any ‘new-manager bounce’, as feared by Reds manager Andoni Iraola, had no time to materialise with a rash challenge from Lenny Yoro on Alexander Isak leading to a straight red in the eighth minute.

Pochettino slammed the decision to send off Yoro after the game, but there was a familiar feeling about the performance overall.

Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at five key takeaways as the opening salvo of the ninth manager since United’s last league title in 2013 fell apart – resulting in the worst start for a new manager of the club in 100 years.

Even though United have greater concerns, the answer was undoubtedly: no. The question for the referee, in sending off Yoro for denying a goalscoring opportunity, had four considerations: distance between the offence and the goal, general direction of the play, likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball, and location and number of defenders.

news.originalContent:
The rise of Cockroach Janta Party and what it reveals about the future of politics and journalism in India.

A youth-led movement born as online satire has unsettled Indian politics. Named after a dismissive remark by the chief justice, the Cockroach Janta Party has mobilised some of the country’s biggest protests in years. They have been driven by anger over exam leaks, unemployment and a lack of political accountability.

The demonstrators have been met by heavy police crackdowns and clashed with mainstream media outlets they accuse of serving the government.

As young Indians turn to social media and independent outlets to tell their stories, this film examines the growing divide between India’s youth and mainstream media and what it could mean for the future of politics and journalism.

Contributors:
Manisha Pande – Editorial director, Newslaundry
Ashutosh Ranka – Co-convenor, Cockroach Janta Party
Rajat Sethi – Visiting fellow, India Foundation
Priyanshi Sharma – Cofounder, Peek TV

On China, US is torn between the fears of the national security establishment and the prospect of expanded trade.

For decades, China was considered the top threat to continued US global primacy, and President Donald Trump’s moves to expand trade with Beijing – even on advanced technology – are rattling Washington’s national security establishment. So when former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued that the US should sell advanced chips to China to maintain dominance over the AI market, the traditional national security hawks baulked. US political scientist Matthew Kroenig tells host Steve Clemons that “the only one who seems to be unworried is President Trump”.

news.originalContent:
Kawas, a democratic socialist, won with 74.5 percent of the vote, championing progressive politics.

New York City, United States – “You have all elected the first Palestinian in New York Senate history!” Aber Kawas shouted over cheers to hundreds of Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) members at a bar on election night.

As chants of “Aber! Aber! Aber!” filled the patio of Bohemia Beer Garden on November 3, media cameras flashed against her shiny blazer, embroidered with traditional Palestinian tatreez in gold and red.

Kawas, 34, made history as the first Palestinian, and the first Muslim woman, in the New York state Senate and the state legislature. She won the seat representing district 12 in northwest Queens, home to one of New York City’s largest Arab communities, where nearly half of residents were born outside the United States.

As her speech ended and chants of “Free, Free Palestine” rang through the garden, Stylianos Karolidis, a DSA organiser on Kawas’s team, stepped up to remind supporters that she really, really had not wanted to run for office. The DSA had to “hound her non-stop” until she acquiesced, he said.

Kawas had worked with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani when he was in the state legislature, so they knew her organising skills.

Kawas said she did not initially think it was possible to run for office without compromising her commitment to Palestinian liberation. Her victory, with 74.5 percent of the vote against Republican Han Khon To, was part of a broader tide of wins for pro-Palestine and democratic socialist candidates in the midterm elections, including Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Mayor-elect Nithya Raman in Los Angeles, California.

“This midterm election showed a politics of human rights that includes Palestinians is a winning platform,” said Institute for Middle East Understanding policy project executive director Margaret DeReus. “For millions of Americans, holding Israel accountable for genocide and supporting Palestinian freedom are the litmus test.”

Days after the election, Kawas reflected on the DSA’s first approach and her doubts about entering a political system she had long distrusted. In her Queens home, a poster honouring Palestinians who had been killed hung above shelves of books on Islamic liberation, the Palestinian movement and US politics. But she ran because the political climate had shifted, she told Al Jazeera.

“It felt like being pro-Palestinian was the most important thing to run on.”

Kawas’s parents were uprooted from their homes in Palestine during the mass expulsions. Her father was uprooted in 1948 and her mother in 1967. They grew up as neighbours in Jordan before falling in love, marrying and moving to the US with their infant son in the 1990s. They later had three daughters. Aber is the third child of the four, sandwiched between her two sisters. “Which is why I have a lot of politician skills,” she said, laughing.

But when she was in the seventh grade, her father was detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), which her mother described as a regular occurrence in New York’s post-9/11 Muslim community. His detention meant weekend visits to prison, and it left the family struggling.

“I had to work whether I wanted to or not; you have to become both man and woman, father and mother,” her mother, Manal Abu Samaha, told Al Jazeera.

When Kawas was a teenager, she said she travelled to Albany to tell her family’s story, hoping to expand opportunities for undocumented students like her older brother, who was ineligible for a college scholarship. Lawmakers seemed uninterested, Kawas recalls.

The state senator-elect credits the experience with launching her advocacy career and shaping her goals as a politician. “It’s not upending systems, but it’s meeting real, immediate material needs for people,” she said. “That’s maybe a little kernel of what got me to run.”

Backed by Mamdani and the DSA, Kawas’s campaign said it mobilised more than 1,000 volunteers to knock on doors, make calls and campaign on affordable housing, healthcare and public transport, as well as the Palestinian solidarity work that has shaped her life.

Kawas recalled that, while Mamdani was warned that supporting Palestine would end his political career, the stance instead helped him earn voters’ trust. Seeing this, she said, made her less wary that entering politics would require her to compromise her beliefs.

“I voted for Aber Kawas because Palestinian liberation is not separate from the everyday survival and basic needs that Americans and New Yorkers struggle with,” said community organiser Doreen Mohammed. “Aber Kawas’s vocal support for Palestine is what we need more of everywhere.”

Kawas told Al Jazeera she believes her stance on Palestine helped her earn trust from local leaders. Whether it can change US policy is a harder question.

“Many of us are rightfully cautious, if not outright sceptical, when it comes to electoral politics,” said Samee Sulaiman, an anthropologist at Columbia University who studies the Middle East. “Can we build and use this nascent power to finally end American support of Israel in every way? This will be the real test.”

Kawas acknowledged that a lot will depend on the political will of legislative leaders.

“The challenge, truly, is going to be the political will of the leadership,” she said. “We [the DSA] are still a minority in the legislature.”

Her first priority is reviving the Not on Our Dime! bill, which she drafted with then-Assembly member Zohran Mamdani in 2023 to prohibit New York non-profits from supporting illegal Israeli settlement activity in the occupied Palestinian territory. Rejected at the time, it is now back before the New York state Senate.

Kawas said she remains convinced change is possible, pointing to the activists who helped bring an end to apartheid in South Africa.

“If there’s the power of the people behind you, that is what you carry with you, and that’s who you’ll be accountable to.”

“Part of a five-story apartment building has ​collapsed following a Russian drone attack, Zelenskiy ​said on X. “I thank our first responders for acting quickly: nine people have already been evacuated, ​and the fire has been contained.”

Local officials ​said four people, including a teenager, were injured.

Emergency service ‌footage ⁠showed rescuers searching through a large pile of rubble, helping residents descend from the damaged building by ladder and crane ​platform.

At 3:35 ​p.m. (1335 GMT) ⁠rescuers had to stop their search for survivors because of ​an incoming aerial threat.

Shortly after, three ​explosions ⁠rang through the town of Dymer, with Reuters footage showing an unidentified aerial object ⁠on ​fire falling from the ​sky. Civilians and rescuers were seen taking shelter in nearby ​buildings.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The NCAA women’s basketball tournament is set to scrap the rule of pregame handshakes between head coaches, per multiple reports Saturday that cited a memo sent by the Division I women’s basketball committee to all D-I programs.

Per the memo, the committee reportedly “encourages” coaches to still shake hands informally ahead of team introductions at the tournament. However, it will no longer be a requirement.

The change comes after the ruling blew up during the women’s Final Four a year ago when Geno Auriemma infamously had a fiery confrontation with Dawn Staley in a postgame handshake line following the Gamecocks’ semifinal victory over the Huskies.

The coaches met at center court along the sidelines to shake hands when suddenly the two started jawing at one another and as things escalated, game officials and team staff got in between the two.

In the immediate aftermath, Staley said “ask Geno” when asked about the incident.

The 12-time national champion head coach went on to explain he took issue with Staley not showing up for their pregame handshake at center court during the coach introductions following the starting lineups. However, photographs later confirmed that they shook hands before the game.

“I waited there for like three minutes,” he said after the game. “So, it is what it is.”

Less than 12 hours later, Auriemma released an apology, stating there was “no excuse” for his outburst.

“It’s unlike what I do and what our standard is here at Connecticut,” he said in a statement. “I want to apologize to the staff and the team at South Carolina. It was uncalled for in how I reacted.”

“The story should be how well South Carolina played and I don’t want my actions to detract from that,” Auriemma added. “I’ve had a great relationship with their staff, and I sincerely want to apologize to them.”

Staley and her Gamecocks went on to lose the final to UCLA, 79-51.

The NCAA’s memo also detailed that game clocks are required to display tenths of a second on shot clocks for the 2027 opening round, first and second rounds of the tournament.

That has already been a requirement at regional games and for the Final Four. By 2028, it will be a requirement for each round.

Additionally, there will no longer be locker room media access nor mandatory press conferences between the Sweet 16 and Elite Eight at the regional locations. Pregame interviews with coaches at those events have also been discarded.

The NCAA men’s and women’s tournaments are expanding to 76 teams in 2027. The top 16 seeds will be revealed on March 13, the day before Selection Sunday.

news.originalContent:
Marc Lamont Hill speaks with tech entrepreneur Anil Dash about AI’s risks and the fight for ethical technology.

The artificial intelligence boom is transforming the global economy and concentrating enormous power in the hands of a few technology companies. But a series of developments is raising new questions about the industry’s stability and accountability from the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy to a wave of technology outages affecting the US government, major banks, companies and aviation systems alongside reports of hacked refrigerators across Europe. Concerns are mounting over the economic risks, mass layoffs, privacy and environmental impact of AI. And as AI company Anthropic began trading publicly, reaching a $2 trillion valuation, questions are mounting over whether the extraordinary levels of AI investment are sustainable. Is there a future where AI can be used for the collective good?

This week on UpFront, Marc Lamont Hill speaks with Anil Dash, former adviser to the White House Office of Digital Strategy in former United States President Barack Obama’s administration, about the risks of the AI boom, Silicon Valley’s growing political influence and the urgent need for greater accountability.

Fans of the Bill Lawrence-verse are experiencing a rare but agonizing drought.

Thankfully, Bad Monkey Season 2 and the return of Scrubs are right around the corner. But Rooster Season 2 won’t premiere for a while. Ted Lasso has yet to be renewed for Season 5. And we miss our Shrinking fam so much it hurts!

Thankfully, Lawrence and co-creators Brett Goldstein and Jason Segel are bringing Apple TV’s Emmy-nominated comedy back for more. And nearly eight months after Shrinking Season 3’s finale left fans and characters craving more, we have some exciting Shrinking Season 4 production updates.

So when is Shrinking Season 4’s release date? What will Shrinking Season 4 be about? How many episodes are in Shrinking Season 4? And who’s joining Shrinking‘s Season 4 cast?

Here’s what to know about the future of Apple TV’s beloved comedy.

Shrinking Season 1 had 10 episodes, Season 2 featured 12 episodes, and Shrinking Season 3 consisted of 11 episodes. (That said, the supersized Episode 1 was essentially the length of two episodes.)

If you’re looking for a detailed Shrinking Season 3 finale recap, Decider’s got you covered. As we said, when the end credits rolled on Season 3, there was a clear sense of closure within the show’s found family, but fans also didn’t want to say goodbye to these beloved characters yet. Thankfully, we didn’t have to!

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Iran unveiled a new underground missile launcher capable of firing two rockets simultaneously, releasing footage of the weapon in what appeared to be a warning to President Trump as Washington weighs renewed military strikes against Tehran.

Videos released Sunday by Iran’s semi-official Fars news agency showed Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) commanders touring a sprawling underground military facility, where the newly displayed launcher was surrounded by rows of missiles and military equipment.

The launcher is designed to fire two liquid-fueled missiles at once, marking the first time Iran has publicly displayed the new system.

Liquid-fueled missiles offer operators greater flexibility to adjust their speed and flight trajectories, while the launcher’s underground location could make the weapons more difficult for US and Israeli forces to detect and destroy.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps aerospace force previously demonstrated a launcher capable of simultaneously firing two solid-fueled missiles on April 7. Sunday’s footage, however, showcased the country’s newly developed liquid-fuel system.

Maj. Gen. Ahmad Vahidi, the IRGC’s commander-in-chief, visited the facility and received briefings on the force’s combat readiness and recent missile developments.

Brig. Gen. Seyyed Majid Mousavi, commander of the IRGC aerospace force, claimed Iran had significantly expanded its military capabilities despite the recent fighting.

“We have integrated ‘surprises’ and highly effective assets into our combat structure,” Mousavi said.

Footage showed Mousavi riding through the underground tunnels in a Jeep as military personnel displayed an extensive collection of missiles and launch equipment.

The video also featured a handwritten message aimed at the White House, declaring: “At the White House, being a b—–d isn’t an insult; it’s a qualification standard.”The display appears intended to counter Washington’s claims that Iran’s missile program has been severely weakened by the conflict and to signal that Tehran retains weapons capable of threatening US and allied forces.

Trump has repeatedly touted the military campaign as a major success, declaring a “very big victory” and describing the war as “effectively over.”

“We’re just keeping it the status quo,” Trump told reporters at the White House earlier this month, while warning that the US remained “locked and loaded” if circumstances changed.

The president also directed Vice President JD Vance to halt negotiations with Iran over its nuclear program.

But the possibility of renewed military action remains on the table.

Trump is reportedly weighing a four-to-seven-day bombing campaign against Iran alongside Israel, according to reports from The New York Times and Axios, following new intelligence about Tehran’s efforts to rebuild its missile capabilities.

The reports came after Roman Gofman, the director of Israel’s Mossad intelligence agency, traveled to Washington and reportedly pressured US officials to consider another round of strikes.

Israel has also warned the White House that Iran is making advances in its chemical and biological weapons programs.

Any renewed American offensive would likely focus on Iran’s missile arsenal, though energy infrastructure and other military facilities could also be targeted.

Iran first released footage of its underground “missile city” earlier this month, showcasing what it described as a vast subterranean weapons network designed to protect its arsenal from aerial attacks.

Among the missiles displayed were the Fattah, which Tehran claims is a hypersonic weapon, and the long-range Khorramshahr missile.

Some weapons in the footage were deliberately blurred, apparently to conceal details of Iran’s remaining military capabilities.

The underground facilities could complicate any future US or Israeli campaign by providing protected storage and launch locations for weapons that may have survived previous strikes.
